question:
A 2-week-old female newborn is brought to the physician because of increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation and weighed 3066 g (6 lb 12 oz); she now weighs 3200 g (7 lb 1 oz). She is exclusively breastfed. Her older brother died 3 months after liver surgery. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 145/min, and respirations are 40/min. Examination shows yellow discoloration extending to the palms and soles. The liver is palpated 1 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hematocrit 51%
Serum
Bilirubin
Total 16.1 mg/dL
Direct 0.7 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 22 U/L
AST 12 U/L
ALT 12 U/L
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "2-week-old newborn" -> "increasing yellow discoloration" -> "jaundice" -> "total bilirubin 16.1 mg/dL" -> "direct bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL" -> "predominantly indirect hyperbilirubinemia" -> "breastfed" -> "breast milk jaundice" -> 70%

CHAIN: "2-week-old newborn" -> "increasing yellow discoloration" -> "jaundice" -> "total bilirubin 16.1 mg/dL" -> "direct bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL" -> "predominantly indirect hyperbilirubinemia" -> "exclusively breastfed" -> "breastfeeding failure jaundice" -> 60%

CHAIN: "2-week-old newborn" -> "increasing yellow discoloration" -> "jaundice" -> "total bilirubin 16.1 mg/dL" -> "direct bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL" -> "predominantly indirect hyperbilirubinemia" -> "older brother died after liver surgery" -> "possible genetic or familial liver condition" -> "biliary atresia" -> 50%

CHAIN: "2-week-old newborn" -> "increasing yellow discoloration" -> "jaundice" -> "total bilirubin 16.1 mg/dL" -> "direct bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL" -> "predominantly indirect hyperbilirubinemia" -> "normal birth weight and gestation" -> "physiologic neonatal jaundice" -> 40%

CHAIN: "2-week-old newborn" -> "increasing yellow discoloration" -> "jaundice" -> "total bilirubin 16.1 mg/dL" -> "direct bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL" -> "predominantly indirect hyperbilirubinemia" -> "no evidence of hemolysis" -> "isoimmune mediated hemolysis unlikely" -> 30%
analysis: The newborn presents with jaundice at 2 weeks of age, with a total bilirubin level of 16.1 mg/dL and a direct bilirubin level of 0.7 mg/dL, indicating predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. The history of an older sibling who died after liver surgery raises suspicion for a genetic or familial condition. The weight gain is appropriate, suggesting adequate breastfeeding. The liver is slightly enlarged, but the liver function tests (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) are normal. Breast milk jaundice typically presents with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in an otherwise healthy, well-fed infant, and usually appears after the first week of life, peaking at 2-3 weeks. The clinical picture and laboratory findings are most consistent with breast milk jaundice.
